statement.text: For $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\tau\in S_m$, where $n\leqslant m$, let $d_n^{\mathrm{flex}}(\sigma,\tau)=(1/n)\cdot(|\{x\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\mid \sigma(x)\ne\tau(x)\}|+(m-n))$. An almost-homomorphism $\{f_n\}$ is said to be flexibly close to a homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms $\rho_n:G\to S_{m_n}$ with $n\leqslant m_n$ such that $d_n^{\mathrm{flex}}(\rho_n(g),f_n(g))\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ for all $g\in G$. The group $G$ is said to be flexibly permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of $G$ is flexibly close to a homomorphism. Is $\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$ flexibly permutation-stable?
